title: Guard block on weakening rules.toml edits
description:
New branch in src/bin/guard.rs run() for `.sutra/rules.toml`, same shape as the Cargo.toml branch (~line 120, before the indexed-file bail): build_proposed_content → parse_rules the proposed TOML in memory → compute constraint IDs + severities → diff against active (unreleased) constraint_ratchets rows via read-only conn. Missing ratcheted ID or severity < floor → blocking deny. Additions and severity increases pass with zero friction (append-only direction). Malformed proposed TOML: deny is tempting but wrong — broken TOML fails parse_rules at load anyway; let it through (constraint_parse_errors channel owns that).

Deny message teaches the ceremony: name + rendered_description + provenance of the ratcheted constraint, why it can't be weakened by edit, and "a human must run `sutra ratchet release <id> --rationale ...` first. To strengthen a ratcheted constraint (e.g. widen scope): release the old ID, then add the replacement."

Sequencing note: touches the same guard files as sutra/243 (pattern arc) — coordinate merge order, no logical dependency.

Design: sutra/223 implementation_plan. Tests in src/guard.rs #[cfg(test)]: deletion denied, severity-lowering denied, addition passes, severity-increase passes, released constraint deletable, non-ratcheted constraint freely editable.

edges.note: both touch src/guard.rs + src/bin/guard.rs — coordinate merge order, no logical dependency
